result.topic_en: A fragment by J. A. Euler that seeks the limiting excess of the asymptote length CN over the hyperbolic arc AM as the point M recedes to infinity, setting the difference up as integrals and series in a substitution variable.
result.transcription:
Fragmentorum ex Adversariis continuatio. 497
100.
(J. A. Euler.)
Problema. (Fig. 64.) Pro hyperbola, cujus semiaxis $AC=a$, posito $AP=x$, $PM=y$, sit $ny=\sqrt{(2ax+xx)}$, *
et ex $M$ ad asymtotam $CN$ ducatur $MN$ axi parallela, invenire excursum rectae $CN$ supra curvam $AM$, quando punctum $M$ in infinitum promovetur.
Posito $x=\infty$ fit $ny=x$, hinc $\tang ACN=\frac{1}{n}$ et $\sin ACN=\frac{1}{\sqrt{(1+nn)}}=\frac{PM}{CN}=\frac{y}{CN}$, ergo $CN=y\sqrt{(1+nn)}$,
Tum vero habemus $nnyy+aa=(a+x)^2$, ergo
$$x=\sqrt{(nnyy+aa)}-a,\quad \text{unde}\quad dx=\frac{nnydy}{\sqrt{(nnyy+aa)}};$$
hinc arcus $AM=\int dy\sqrt{\left(1+nn-\frac{nnaa}{nnyy+aa}\right)}$. Hinc
$$CN-AM=\int dy\left(\sqrt{(nn+1)}-\sqrt{\left(nn+1-\frac{nnaa}{nnyy+aa}\right)}\right).$$
Ponatur nunc $v=\sqrt{(nn+1)}-\sqrt{\left(nn+1-\frac{nnaa}{nnyy+aa}\right)}$, erit
$$\frac{-nnaa}{nnyy+aa}=-2v\sqrt{(nn+1)}+vv,\quad \text{sive}$$
$$\frac{1}{2v\sqrt{(nn+1)}-vv}=\frac{yy}{aa}+\frac{1}{nn},\quad \text{ergo}$$
$$y=\frac{a}{n}\sqrt{\frac{nn-2v\sqrt{(nn+1)}+vv}{2v\sqrt{(nn+1)}-vv}}.$$
Per logarithmos autem erit
$$2ly-2la=l\left(nn-2v\sqrt{(nn+1)}+vv\right)-2ln-l\left(2v\sqrt{(nn+1)}-vv\right)$$
$$\frac{dy}{y}=\frac{-dv\sqrt{(1+nn)}+vdv}{nn-2v\sqrt{(nn+1)}+vv}-\frac{dv\sqrt{(nn+1)}+vdv}{2v\sqrt{(nn+1)}-vv}$$
hinc autem vix quicquam concludi poterit.
Ineamus ergo aliam viam: Cum sit
$$CN-AM=\sqrt{(nn+1)}\int dy\left(1-\sqrt{\left(1-\frac{nnaa}{nn+1}\cdot\frac{1}{nnyy+aa}\right)}\right),$$
sit $\frac{nnaa}{nn+1}\cdot\frac{1}{nnyy+aa}=\cos^2\varphi$, erit $nnyy+aa=\frac{nnaa}{(nn+1)\cos^2\varphi}$, hinc
$$ny=\frac{a\sqrt{(nn\sin^2\varphi-\cos^2\varphi)}}{\cos\varphi\sqrt{(nn+1)}},$$
ubi casu $y=0$ erit $\cos^2\varphi=\frac{nn}{nn+1}$ et $\cos\varphi=\frac{n}{\sqrt{(nn+1)}}$ et $\sin\varphi=\frac{1}{\sqrt{(nn+1)}}$, $\tang\varphi=\frac{1}{n}$, hinc $\varphi=ACN$, et pro $y=\infty$ erit $\varphi=90^\circ$. Ergo integrari debet a $\varphi=ACN$, vel $\tang\varphi=\frac{1}{n}$, usque ad $\varphi=90^\circ$, vel $\tang\varphi=\infty$.
Est autem $ny=\frac{a\sqrt{(nn\tang^2\varphi-1)}}{\sqrt{(nn+1)}}$. Ponatur $\tang\varphi=t$ et integrandum a $t=\frac{1}{n}$ usque ad $t=\infty$; at $\sin\varphi=\frac{t}{\sqrt{(1+tt)}}$. Hinc $CN-AM=\sqrt{(1+nn)}\cdot\frac{ann}{n\sqrt{(nn+1)}}\int\frac{tdt}{\sqrt{(nntt-1)}}\left(1-\frac{t}{\sqrt{(1+tt)}}\right)$, vel
$$CN-AM=\frac{a}{n}\sqrt{(nntt-1)}-\frac{a}{n}\int\frac{nnttdt}{\sqrt{(tt+1)(nntt-1)}}.$$
Est autem $\frac{1}{\sqrt{(1+tt)}}=(1+tt)^{-\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{1}{t}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{t^3}+\frac{1.3}{2.4}\cdot\frac{1}{t^5}-\frac{1.3.5}{2.4.6}\cdot\frac{1}{t^7}+$ etc.
Erit $CN-AM=na\left(\frac{1}{2}\int\frac{dt}{t\sqrt{(nntt-1)}}-\frac{1.3}{2.4}\int\frac{dt}{t^3\sqrt{(nntt-1)}}+\frac{1.3.5}{2.4.6}\int\frac{dt}{t^5\sqrt{(nntt-1)}}-\text{etc.}\right)$. Ubi notandum si
L. Euleri Op. posthuma. T. I. 63

items.quote: Pro hyperbola, cujus semiaxis $AC=a$, posito $AP=x$, $PM=y$, sit $ny=\sqrt{(2ax+xx)}$, et ex $M$ ad asymtotam $CN$ ducatur $MN$ axi parallela, invenire excursum rectae $CN$ supra curvam $AM$, quando punctum $M$ in infinitum promovetur.
items.english: For a hyperbola with semiaxis AC = a, setting AP = x and PM = y, let ny = sqrt(2ax + xx). From M draw MN parallel to the axis to the asymptote CN. Find the excess of the line CN over the curve AM when the point M is moved off to infinity.

items.quote: hinc autem vix quicquam concludi poterit.
items.english: From this, however, hardly anything can be concluded.
